arxiv-2101-03746.title: Bounds on GUP parameters from GW150914 and GW190521
arxiv-2101-03746.creator: Ashmita Das, Saurya Das, Noor R. Mansour, Elias C. Vagenas
arxiv-2101-03746.description: Abstract We compute bounds on the GUP parameters for two versions of GUP using gravitational wave data from the events GW150914 and GW190521. The speed of the graviton and photon are calculated in a curved spacetime modified by GUP, assuming that these particles have a small mass.

arxiv-2112-15459.title: Social Neuro AI: Social Interaction as the "dark matter" of AI
arxiv-2112-15459.creator: Samuele Bolotta, Guillaume Dumas
arxiv-2112-15459.description: Abstract This article introduces a three-axis framework indicating how AI can be informed by biological examples of social learning mechanisms. We argue that the complex human cognitive architecture owes a large portion of its expressive power to its ability to engage in social and cultural learning. However, the field of AI has mostly embraced a solipsistic perspective on intelligence.

arxiv-2212-14613.title: Delving into Semantic Scale Imbalance
arxiv-2212-14613.creator: Yanbiao Ma, Licheng Jiao, Fang Liu, Yuxin Li, Shuyuan Yang, Xu Liu Key Laboratory of Intelligent Perception and Image Understanding of the Ministry of Education Xidian University Xi’an, 710071, China { ybmamail,yxli_12 } @stu.xidian.edu.cn, lchjiao@mail.xidian.edu.cn, f63liu@163.com, syyang@xidian.e
arxiv-2212-14613.description: Abstract Model bias triggered by long-tailed data has been widely studied. However, measure based on the number of samples cannot explicate three phenomena simultaneously: (1) Given enough data, the classification performance gain is marginal with additional samples. ​(2) Classification performance decays precipitously as the number of training samples decreases when there is insufficient data.

arxiv-2302-00687.title: Euclid preparation. XXXII. Evaluating the weak lensing cluster mass biases using the Three Hundred Project hydrodynamical simulations
arxiv-2302-00687.creator: Euclid Collaboration: C. Giocoli 1,2, M. Meneghetti 1,2, E. Rasia 3,4, S. Borgani 3,5,6,4, G. Despali 7, G. F. Lesci 8,1, F. Marulli 8,1,2, L. Moscardini 8,1,2, M. Sereno 1,2, W. Cui 9,10,11, A. Knebe 9,10,12, G. Yepes 9,10, T. Castro 3,6,4, P.-S. Corasaniti 13, S. Pires 14, G. Castignani 8,1, T. Sc
arxiv-2302-00687.description: Abstract The photometric catalogue of galaxy clusters extracted from ESA Euclid data is expected to be very competitive for cosmological studies. Using state-of-the-art hydrodynamical simulations, we present systematic analyses simulating the expected weak lensing profiles from clusters in a variety of dynamic states and at wide range of redshifts.

arxiv-2306-02793.title: Verification of ultrafast spin transfer effects in FeNi alloys
arxiv-2306-02793.creator: Christina Möller, Henrike Probst, G. S. Matthijs Jansen, Maren Schumacher, Mariana Brede, John Kay Dewhurst, Marcel Reutzel, Daniel Steil, Sangeeta Sharma, Stefan Mathias
arxiv-2306-02793.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Christina Möller, Henrike Probst, G. S. Matthijs Jansen, Maren Schumacher, Mariana Brede, John Kay Dewhurst, Marcel Reutzel, Daniel Steil, Sangeeta Sharma, Stefan Mathias. The optical intersite spin transfer (OISTR) effect was recently verified in Fe 50 Ni 50 using magneto-optical Kerr measurements in the extreme ultraviolet range.

arxiv-2308-03415.title: End-to-End Evaluation for Low-Latency Simultaneous Speech Translation
arxiv-2308-03415.creator: Christian Huber, Tu Anh Dinh, Carlos Mullov, Ngoc Quan Pham, Thai Binh Nguyen, Fabian Retkowski, Stefan Constantin, Enes Yavuz Ugan, Danni Liu, Zhaolin Li, Sai Koneru, Jan Niehues, Alexander Waibel
arxiv-2308-03415.description: Abstract The challenge of low-latency speech translation has recently draw significant interest in the research community as shown by several publications and shared tasks. Therefore, it is essential to evaluate these different approaches in realistic scenarios. However, currently only specific aspects of the systems are evaluated and often it is not possible to compare different approaches.

arxiv-2406-14951.title: An Idiosyncrasy of Time-discretization in Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2406-14951.creator: Kris De Asis, Richard S. Sutton
arxiv-2406-14951.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kris De Asis, Richard S. Sutton. Many reinforcement learning algorithms are built on an assumption that an agent interacts with an environment over fixed-duration, discrete time steps. However, physical systems are continuous in time, requiring a choice of time-discretization granularity when digitally controlling them. Furthermore, such systems do not wait for decisions to be made before advancing the environment state, necessitating the study of how the choice of discretization may affect a reinforcement learning algorithm.

arxiv-2501-01450.title: Real-Time Computational Visual Aberration Correcting Display Through High-Contrast Inverse Blurring.
arxiv-2501-01450.creator: Akhilesh Balaji, Dhruv Ramu
arxiv-2501-01450.description: Abstract This paper presents a framework for developing a live vision-correcting display (VCD) to address refractive visual aberrations without the need for traditional vision correction devices like glasses or contact lenses, particularly in scenarios where wearing them may be inconvenient.

arxiv-2502-04818.title: Harnessing omnipresent oscillator networks as computational resource
arxiv-2502-04818.creator: Thomas Geert de Jong, Hirofumi Notsu, Kohei Nakajima
arxiv-2502-04818.description: Abstract Abstract: Nature is pervaded with oscillatory dynamics. In networks of coupled oscillators patterns can arise when the system synchronizes to an external input. Hence, these networks provide processing and memory of input. We present a universal framework for harnessing oscillator networks as computational resource. This computing framework is introduced by the ubiquitous model for phase-locking, the Kuramoto model.

arxiv-2505-18492.title: Formally Solving Answer-Construction Problems in Lean
arxiv-2505-18492.creator: Jialiang Sun, Yuzhi Tang, Ao Li, Chris Maddison, Kuldeep Meel
arxiv-2505-18492.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in formal mathematical reasoning. Mathematical competition problems fall into two broad types: theorem-proving problems ask for a proof of a fully specified statement, whereas answer-construction problems ask the solver to construct an answer object and prove that it satisfies the stated specification.

arxiv-2506-09282.title: ScalableHD: Scalable and High-Throughput Hyperdimensional Computing Inference on Multi-Core CPUs
arxiv-2506-09282.creator: Dhruv Parikh, Viktor Prasanna
arxiv-2506-09282.description: Abstract Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) is a brain-inspired computing paradigm that represents and manipulates information using high-dimensional vectors, called hypervectors (HV). Traditional HDC methods, while robust to noise and inherently parallel, rely on single-pass, non-parametric training and often suffer from low accuracy. To address this, recent approaches adopt iterative training of base and class HVs, typically accelerated on GPUs.

arxiv-2508-15546.title: Robust Self-Testing of Multiqudit Supersinglet Slater States via Constant Number of Binary Measurements
arxiv-2508-15546.creator: Arturo Konderak, Wojciech Bruzda, Remigiusz Augusiak
arxiv-2508-15546.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arturo Konderak, Wojciech Bruzda, Remigiusz Augusiak. Self-testing is a powerful device-independent technique that enables one to deduce the forms of both the quantum state and the measurements involved in a physical experiment based solely on observed correlations. Although numerous schemes for self-testing multipartite entangled states have been proposed, they are typically difficult to implement experimentally, as their complexity increases significantly with the number of subsystems or the local dimension.

arxiv-2512-24293.title: Quasi Neighborhood Balanced Coloring of Graphs
arxiv-2512-24293.description: Abstract For a simple graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) , a coloring of vertices of G G using two colors, say red and blue, is called a quasi neighborhood balanced coloring if, for every vertex of the graph, the number of red neighbors and the number of blue neighbors differ by at most one.

arxiv-2602-11136.title: FormalJudge : A Neuro-Symbolic Paradigm for Agentic Oversight
arxiv-2602-11136.creator: Jiayi Zhou, Yang Sheng, Hantao Lou, Yaodong Yang, Jie Fu
arxiv-2602-11136.description: Abstract As LLM-based agents increasingly operate in high-stakes domains with real-world consequences, ensuring their behavioral safety becomes paramount. The dominant oversight paradigm, LLM-as-a-Judge , faces a fundamental dilemma: how can probabilistic systems reliably supervise other probabilistic systems without inheriting their failure modes?

pmc-10573438.title: Failure Rate of Medical Treatment for Miscarriage Correlated with the Difference between Gestational Age According to Last Menstrual Period and Gestational Size Calculated via Ultrasound
pmc-10573438.creator: Ohad Gluck, Elad Barber, Matan Friedman, Ohad Feldstein, Ori Tal, Ehud Grinstein, Yossi Mizrachi, Ram Kerner, Michal Saidian, Mai Menasherof, Ron Sagiv
pmc-10573438.description: Objective: To study whether the interval between gestational age calculated using the last menstrual period (GA-LMP) and gestational age calculated via ultrasound (GA-US) is correlated with the success rate of medical treatment in cases of miscarriages. Methods: This was a retrospective cohort study conducted in a gynecology unit in a tertiary medical center.

pmc-10594965.title: Nickel-related hypersensitivity reactions following endovascular interventions: A review of current evidence
pmc-10594965.creator: Vanessa H Tjen, Paul Zichu Yang
pmc-10594965.description: Introduction:Nickel is a principal alloying agent in the production of vascular endoprostheses, despite persisting as the most habitually identified allergen. Variable nickel-related hypersensitivity manifestations following endovascular intervention were reported, challenging established paradigms in treatment and accuracy of prognostic assessments. The objective of this review is to critically evaluate current metrics to maximise patient-related outcomes.

pmc-11516508.title: Associations between general practice and outpatient care continuity in people with multimorbidity
pmc-11516508.creator: T Beaney, J Clarke, T Woodcock, M Barahona, A Majeed, P Aylin
pmc-11516508.description: BackgroundRelational continuity in primary and secondary care is linked to better health outcomes for patients, but it is unclear whether metrics of continuity in each setting are associated. Our study examined the association between relational continuity in general practice (GP) and continuity of hospital outpatient specialties in people with clusters of multimorbidity.

pmc-11688726.title: UNVEILING THE DIFFERENTIAL IMPACT OF NEGATIVE AND POSITIVE AFFECT ON SUBJECTIVE COGNITIVE PERCEPTIONS
pmc-11688726.creator: Jacklyn Gehling, Hannah Marx, Ravneet Dhaliwal, Steven Harris, Frank Robertson, Claudia Jacova Chenoweth
pmc-11688726.description: Subjective Cognitive Decline (SCD) is a state of perceived decline in cognitive abilities that may mark Alzheimer’s disease onset and may be influenced by affective and personality factors. This study aimed to examine the distinct impact of negative and positive affect on SCD burden in older adults. The sample included 279 cognitively healthy, community-dwelling participants, aged 60-96 (M=73.

pmc-12407425.title: Fracture fixation in the hand and wrist: A 16-year population-based study of 56 163 patients from the Swedish National Patient Register
pmc-12407425.creator: Viktor Schmidt, Elsa Pihl, Cecilia Mellstrand Navarro, Michael Axenhus, Ken Iseri, Ken Iseri, Ken Iseri
pmc-12407425.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Hand and wrist fractures are among the most common orthopaedic injuries, with a growing trend toward surgical treatment. However, large-scale data on regional variations and treatment trends remain limited. This population-based study analyses the incidence, trends, and regional variations in hand and wrist fracture fixation with plates and screws in Sweden from 2008 to 2023, with predictive modelling for future trends. A total of 56,163 patients aged ≥15 years underwent fixation (code NDJ69).

pmc-12408411.title: The role of 3D printing in skeletal muscle-on-a-chip models: Current applications and future potential
pmc-12408411.creator: Wei Bao, Junyan Liu, Chengcheng Du, Senrui Liu, Jiacheng Liu, Zhenglin Zhu, Liangbin Zhou, Zhong Alan Li, Wei Huang, Yiting Lei
pmc-12408411.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Organ-on-a-chip (OoC) systems can simulate the key functions of human organs, combining microfluidics, cell culture, and biomaterials. 3D printing can be integrated into these technologies to facilitate the construction of OoC models. The high precision and layer-by-layer fabrication process of 3D printing not only enables the creation of complex structures for the microfluidic chip but also improves the cellular microenvironment within the chip by harnessing bioinks for 3D bioprinting.

pmc-12538745.title: Lumbar plexus combined with sacral plexus nerve block anesthesia in elderly patients undergoing hip surgery
pmc-12538745.creator: Zhongping Cao
pmc-12538745.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Fractures of hip-related areas are common orthopedic conditions among elderly individuals. Prolonged bed rest can easily lead to life-threatening pulmonary infections, pressure ulcers, lower limb thrombosis, and embolism complications. The most common treatment is hip joint surgery. However, the selection of anesthesia methods for hip surgery in elderly individuals is difficult, these patients often present with multiple comorbidities, including cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases.

pmc-12594642.title: Indirect cognitive mapping in glioma surgery in patients not eligible for awake craniotomy – how I do it
pmc-12594642.creator: Patrick Vigren, Hans Lindehammar
pmc-12594642.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This paper illustrates a method to map cognitive subcortical white matter pathways in brain tumour surgery, in patients not eligible for awake intraoperative mapping. The latter being the gold standard, it is not feasible in all patients.

pmc-12665265.title: Effects of creatine supplementation on muscle strength gains—a meta-analysis and systematic review
pmc-12665265.creator: Haoda Zhang, Tian Lan, Xueru Yan, Haoran Gu, Yanhong Li, Enpeng He
pmc-12665265.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Creatine (Cr) is a widely utilized nutritional supplement. Empirical evidence indicates that Cr supplementation significantly elevates intramuscular Cr content, thereby providing an energy substrate reservoir for exercise performance and facilitating improvements in muscle strength. Although numerous studies have examined the relationship between Cr and muscle strength, comprehensive investigations into population-specific ergogenic responses, optimal Cr dosage, and concomitant training intensity remain limited. These parameters are critical determinants for maximizing the efficacy of Cr supplementation.

pmc-13220285.title: High medical costs and resource shortages constrain rural happiness more than physical access in rural China
pmc-13220285.creator: Yuchen He, Shan Jin, Jing Chen
pmc-13220285.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionAccess to healthcare services is closely associated with people’s subjective well-being (SWB). pmc-13265163.title: Identification of protein lysine lactylation and potential targets in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-13265163.creator: Hanlu Zhang, Xiuji Yan, Lucheng Xi, Sicheng Chen, Qixin Shang, Long-Qi Chen, Wen-Ping Wang
pmc-13265163.description: BackgroundEsophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is one of the most common malignancies with high morbidity and mortality. Exploring the molecular pathogenesis of ESCC is of pivotal importance to improve patients’ prognosis. Lactate-mediated lysine lactylation (Kla) is a novel post-translational modification and critical for cancer progression. However, the role and mechanism of Kla in ESCC metastasis are poorly defined.

pmc-13313914.title: Assessment of Salmonella spp. Lipopolysaccharide immunogenicity for candidate vaccine development
pmc-13313914.creator: Husain Ali Khalaf, Alaa Abdulaziz Abed
pmc-13313914.description: Background: Salmonella infections impose considerable global health challenges, mostly due to the variable serovar efficacy of existing vaccines. Salmonella’s lipopolysaccharide (LPS), an integral surface component that potently stimulates and activates the innate immune system, is a prime candidate for the development of universal vaccine formulations.
